sections.wikitext:

Rodney Jerkins and Julie Frost composed the basis of the song together, with Jerkins on piano and Frost contributing the lyrics and topline melody.<ref name="hitquarters">{{cite web |url=http://www.hitquarters.com/index.php3?page=intrview/opar/intrview_JFrost_interview.html |title=Interview With Julie Frost |publisher=[[HitQuarters]]|date=February 14, 2011 |access-date=May 2, 2011}}</ref> Jerkins' production team, composed of [[Tommy Brown (record producer)|Tommy Brown]] and Jabbar "Bah" Stevens, then worked on the producing the track and contributing to the music composition before will.i.am and Black Eyed Peas; in the words of Frost, the latter "cut it up and gave it their own twist".<ref name="hitquarters"/>

Member apl.de.ap told ''Beatweek Magazine'' that he wanted the song to be the follow-up to "[[The Time (Dirty Bit)]]", because "It's a different tempo and it's also paying homage to the ladies".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.songfacts.com/detail.php?id=21982 |title=Just Can't get enough background |access-date=July 13, 2016}}</ref>

sections.text:
The Beginning{{'}}s second single was announced on Black Eyed Peas' official website on January 21, 2011.

Rodney Jerkins and Julie Frost composed the basis of the song together, with Jerkins on piano and Frost contributing the lyrics and topline melody. Jerkins' production team, composed of Tommy Brown and Jabbar "Bah" Stevens, then worked on the producing the track and contributing to the music composition before will.i.am and Black Eyed Peas; in the words of Frost, the latter "cut it up and gave it their own twist".

Member apl.de.ap told Beatweek Magazine that he wanted the song to be the follow-up to "The Time (Dirty Bit)", because "It's a different tempo and it's also paying homage to the ladies".

Group member Taboo explained the meaning of the song to MTV News as: "The message is knowing that when you're gone from somebody, especially when you're on tour, you can't get enough of them or you're just thinking about them and you just want to let them know that you're always there for them".

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Andy Gill from ''[[The Independent]]'' said, positively, that: "other highlights include "Just Can't Get Enough" – not [[Just Can't Get Enough (Depeche Mode song)|the Depeche Mode song]] – which vaults suddenly from the rare dignity of string-synth textures to a sweatily pumping techno finale".<ref>{{cite news|title=Album: Black Eyed Peas – The Beginning (Interscope/Polydor)|first=Andy|last=Gill|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/reviews/album-black-eyed-peas-the-beginning-interscopepolydor-2143857.html|access-date=February 9, 2011|location=London|work=The Independent|date=November 26, 2010}}</ref> Lewis Corner from [[Digital Spy]] rated it three stars (out of five) and commented that: "The back-and-forth production – reminiscent of vintage arcade game ''[[Pong]]'' – comprises electronic synths and soft strings teamed with heavy beats and, of course, the obligatory vocoded 'mega switch up' – prompting its transformation into a thumping techno endgame. Throw in some 'LOL' text lingo and computerised vocals, and we can't help but think he's perhaps spent a little too much time in front of the PC for this one. You want to be careful Will, we hear they make your eyes go square".<ref>{{cite web|title=Just Can't Get Enough – BEP – Digital Soy (Review)|first=Lewis|last=Corner|website=[[Digital Spy]]|date=March 3, 2011|url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/music/singlesreviews/a306707/the-black-eyed-peas-just-cant-get-enough.html|access-date=March 19, 2011}}</ref>

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The music video for "Just Can't Get Enough" was directed by Ben Mor.<ref name="Zap">{{cite news|url=http://blog.zap2it.com/pop2it/2011/03/black-eyed-peas-just-cant-get-enough-watch-the-video-shot-in-japan-just-1-week-before-tragedy.html|title=Black Eyed Peas' 'Just Can't Get Enough': Watch the video shot in Japan just 1 week before tragedy|last=Schillaci|first=Sophie|date=March 17, 2011|publisher=[[Tribune Media Services]]|work=[[Zap2it]]|access-date=March 23, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110321012742/http://blog.zap2it.com/pop2it/2011/03/black-eyed-peas-just-cant-get-enough-watch-the-video-shot-in-japan-just-1-week-before-tragedy.html|archive-date=March 21, 2011}}</ref> It was shot over a three-day period in Tokyo, Japan primarily in the [[Ginza]] and [[Shibuya]] districts while the group was on a press tour.<ref name="ET">{{cite news|url=http://www.etonline.com/music/108772_Black_Eyed_Peas_Film_New_Video_in_Japan_a_Week_Before_Disaster/ |title=Black Eyed Peas Film New Video in Japan a Week Before Disaster |work=[[Entertainment Tonight]] |publisher=[[CBS Television Studios|CBS Studios]] |date=March 15, 2011 |first=Melissa |last=Reisor |access-date=March 23, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110320204341/http://www.etonline.com/music/108772_Black_Eyed_Peas_Film_New_Video_in_Japan_a_Week_Before_Disaster/ |archive-date=March 20, 2011 }}</ref> The opening clips show shots of the Ginza district. The video was shot between March 3–5, 2011, just one week before the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami.<ref name="Zap"/> In an interview with ''[[Entertainment Tonight]]'', Fergie spoke of the clip and the natural disaster in Japan, saying, "It was the easiest video I ever shot because it was us living our lives. I love that it's showing a true perspective of how it can sometimes be lonely on the road away from our loved ones. It also demonstrates the love and connection we have with Japan. Our heart goes out to all of the Japanese people who have been affected by this natural disaster."<ref name="ET"/> Taboo was also quoted saying "It was an amazing moment in time because Japan has always been my favorite place on the planet. It was great to do our video there. God bless the Japanese. Our love goes out to them."<ref name="ET"/>

[[File:Skyscrapers of Shinjuku 2009 January.jpg|right|thumb|Tokyo, where the music video was filmed.|260px]]

The video premiered on March 16, 2011, on music video website [[Vevo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vevo.com/watch/black-eyed-peas/just-cant-get-enough/USUV71100323|title=Just Can't Get Enough – Black Eyed Peas|work=[[Vevo]]|access-date=March 23, 2011}}</ref> It opens with the translator voice tells the caption "This video was filmed in Japan one week before the earthquake and tsunami. Our thoughts and prayers go out to all the people of Japan. We love you."<ref name="EW">{{cite magazine|url=http://music-mix.ew.com/2011/03/17/black-eyed-peas-just-cant-get-enough/|title=Black Eyed Peas' new 'Just Can't Get Enough' video, set in Tokyo: Watch it here|last=Lufkin|first=Bryan|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|publisher=[[Time Inc]]|date=March 17, 2011|access-date=March 23, 2011}}</ref> It was shot in a [[Guerrilla filmmaking|guerrilla]]-style.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rap-up.com/2011/03/16/video-black-eyed-peas-just-cant-get-enough/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110319142752/http://www.rap-up.com/2011/03/16/video-black-eyed-peas-just-cant-get-enough/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 19, 2011|title=Video: Black Eyed Peas – 'Just Can't Get Enough'|work=[[Rap-Up]]|date=March 16, 2011|access-date=March 23, 2011}}</ref> Fergie is seen overlooking the city from her suite in The Peninsula Tokyo, will.i.am is in the back of a car. Taboo sings his verse while walking in the Shibuya district and apl.de.ap sings his "switched up" verse in front of a futuristic backdrop with flashing lights. It also includes vignettes of Tokyo's nightlife, such as young club-goers taking photos with mobile phones and the city's rail system. At a couple points, it shows all four members wearing different styles of sunglasses and dressed in black performing at a nightclub.<ref name="EW"/> The clip closes with the translator voice with a message to encourage viewers to donate to the [[International Committee of the Red Cross|Red Cross]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1659997/black-eyed-peas-japan-relief.jhtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110319041012/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1659997/black-eyed-peas-japan-relief.jhtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 19, 2011|title=Black Eyed Peas 'Just Can't Get Enough' Video To Aid Japan Disaster Relief|date=March 16, 2011|access-date=March 23, 2011|last=Vena|first= Jocelyn|work=[[MTV News]]|publisher=[[MTV Networks]]}}</ref>

The video received positive reviews from critics. Bill Lamb of [[Dotdash|About.com]] wrote that "The feel ... was already a bit melancholy depicting the loneliness and separation of being on the road. However, the fact that the clip was filmed in Tokyo, Japan just a week before the recent devastating earthquake gives the video even more depth and poignance."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://top40.about.com/b/2011/03/21/black-eyed-peas-release-poignant-just-cant-get-enough-video-filmed-in-japan-just-before-the-earthquake.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716050039/http://top40.about.com/b/2011/03/21/black-eyed-peas-release-poignant-just-cant-get-enough-video-filmed-in-japan-just-before-the-earthquake.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 16, 2012|title=Black Eyed Peas Release Poignant "Just Can't Get Enough" Video Filmed In Japan Just Before the Earthquake|last=Lamb|first=Bill|date=March 21, 2011|work=[[Dotdash|About.com]]|publisher=[[The New York Times Company]]|access-date=March 23, 2011}}</ref> Becky Bain of ''[[Idolator (website)|Idolator]]'' wrote that "It's basically ''[[Lost in Translation (film)|Lost in Translation]]'' with a more thumping soundtrack."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://idolator.com/5798492/the-black-eyed-peas-just-cant-get-enough-video|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715022756/http://idolator.com/5798492/the-black-eyed-peas-just-cant-get-enough-video|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 15, 2012|title=The Black Eyed Peas Tour Tokyo In "Just Can't Get Enough" Video|date=March 18, 2011|last=Bain|first=Becky|work=[[Idolator (website)|Idolator]]|publisher=[[Buzz Media]]|access-date=March 23, 2011}}</ref>
sections.text:
The music video for "Just Can't Get Enough" was directed by Ben Mor. It was shot over a three-day period in Tokyo, Japan primarily in the Ginza and Shibuya districts while the group was on a press tour. The opening clips show shots of the Ginza district. The video was shot between March 3–5, 2011, just one week before the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami. In an interview with Entertainment Tonight, Fergie spoke of the clip and the natural disaster in Japan, saying, "It was the easiest video I ever shot because it was us living our lives. I love that it's showing a true perspective of how it can sometimes be lonely on the road away from our loved ones. It also demonstrates the love and connection we have with Japan. Our heart goes out to all of the Japanese people who have been affected by this natural disaster." Taboo was also quoted saying "It was an amazing moment in time because Japan has always been my favorite place on the planet. It was great to do our video there. God bless the Japanese. Our love goes out to them."

right|thumb|Tokyo, where the music video was filmed.|260px

The video premiered on March 16, 2011, on music video website Vevo. It opens with the translator voice tells the caption "This video was filmed in Japan one week before the earthquake and tsunami. Our thoughts and prayers go out to all the people of Japan. We love you." It was shot in a guerrilla-style. Fergie is seen overlooking the city from her suite in The Peninsula Tokyo, will.i.am is in the back of a car. Taboo sings his verse while walking in the Shibuya district and apl.de.ap sings his "switched up" verse in front of a futuristic backdrop with flashing lights. It also includes vignettes of Tokyo's nightlife, such as young club-goers taking photos with mobile phones and the city's rail system. At a couple points, it shows all four members wearing different styles of sunglasses and dressed in black performing at a nightclub. The clip closes with the translator voice with a message to encourage viewers to donate to the Red Cross.

The video received positive reviews from critics. Bill Lamb of About.com wrote that "The feel ... was already a bit melancholy depicting the loneliness and separation of being on the road. However, the fact that the clip was filmed in Tokyo, Japan just a week before the recent devastating earthquake gives the video even more depth and poignance." Becky Bain of Idolator wrote that "It's basically Lost in Translation with a more thumping soundtrack."

sections.heading: Live performances
sections.wikitext: Black Eyed Peas performed the song for the first time on the [[American Idol (season 10)|tenth season]] of ''[[American Idol]]'' on March 17, 2011.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Lipshutz|first=Jason|date=March 17, 2011|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/karen-rodriguez-voted-off-american-idol-top-11-remain-472475/|title=Karen Rodriguez Voted Off 'American Idol,' Top 11 Remain – Billboard|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref> The performance began with will.i.am, wearing a white suit and playing on the piano and dedicating the song to Japan. Fergie then opened the song while sitting atop the piano wearing a white halter dress. Later, will.i.am stood up and joined her on stage to sing his lines. apl.de.ap and Taboo, also wearing white clothing, sang and rapped along. Behind them, string players and dancers performed, and couples acted out skits. Near the end, the group jumped around on stage, while encouraging the audience to dance and clap along.<ref name="MTV-Video">{{cite news|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1660172/bep-just-cant-get-enough-american-idol.jhtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110320213607/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1660172/bep-just-cant-get-enough-american-idol.jhtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 20, 2011|title=Black Eyed Peas Debut 'Just Can't Get Enough' On 'American Idol'|date=March 17, 2011|access-date=March 23, 2011|last=Carter|first= Kelley L.|work=[[MTV News]]|publisher=[[MTV Networks]]}}</ref> They also performed "Just Can't Get Enough" at the Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards 2011 and in the show that they performed for MTV World Stage. On December 11, 2019, they again performed "Just Can't Get Enough" at the closing ceremony of the [[2019 Southeast Asian Games]] at the [[New Clark City Athletics Stadium]] in Philippines.
sections.text: Black Eyed Peas performed the song for the first time on the tenth season of American Idol on March 17, 2011. The performance began with will.i.am, wearing a white suit and playing on the piano and dedicating the song to Japan. Fergie then opened the song while sitting atop the piano wearing a white halter dress. Later, will.i.am stood up and joined her on stage to sing his lines. apl.de.ap and Taboo, also wearing white clothing, sang and rapped along. Behind them, string players and dancers performed, and couples acted out skits. Near the end, the group jumped around on stage, while encouraging the audience to dance and clap along. They also performed "Just Can't Get Enough" at the Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards 2011 and in the show that they performed for MTV World Stage. On December 11, 2019, they again performed "Just Can't Get Enough" at the closing ceremony of the 2019 Southeast Asian Games at the New Clark City Athletics Stadium in Philippines.
